claims.text: Donepezil: likely exaggerates succinylcholine-type muscle relaxation during anesthesia;
claims.quote: is likely to exaggerate succinylcholine-type muscle relaxation during anesthesia.

claims.text: expect a synergistic effect with succinylcholine, similar neuromuscular blockers or cholinergic agonists (eg, bethanechol).
claims.quote: A synergistic effect may be expected when cholinesterase inhibitors are given concurrently with succinylcholine, similar neuromuscular blocking agents, or cholinergic agonists such as bethanechol.
claims.locator: 7.2 Use with Cholinomimetics and Other Cholinesterase Inhibitors

claims.text: Monitor closely for active or occult GI bleeding, especially with ulcer risk (eg, ulcer history, concurrent NSAIDs).
claims.quote: patients should be monitored closely for symptoms of active or occult gastrointestinal bleeding, especially those at increased risk for developing ulcers, e.g., those with a history of ulcer disease or those receiving concurrent nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
claims.locator: 5.4 Peptic Ulcer Disease and GI Bleeding

claims.text: Overdose: cholinergic crisis (severe N/V, salivation, sweating, bradycardia, hypotension, respiratory depression, collapse, convulsions); increasing muscle weakness may cause death if respiratory muscles are involved.
claims.quote: Overdosage with cholinesterase inhibitors can result in cholinergic crisis characterized by severe nausea, vomiting, salivation, sweating, bradycardia, hypotension, respiratory depression, collapse, and convulsions. Increasing muscle weakness is a possibility and may result in death if respiratory muscles are involved.

claims.text: Tertiary anticholinergics such as atropine may be used as an antidote.
claims.quote: Tertiary anticholinergics such as atropine may be used as an antidote for ARICEPT overdosage.
